chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: Dating the broadcast, "My Little Brown Book" and "Lush Life"
summary: He estimates the date and discusses why "Lush Life" is a complete story rather than a jam vehicle.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: How close can you come to it?

Well, I would say it had to be at least three months before Duke made a record of it, so you could trace back from that. And we also had "My Little Brown Book," another one of Strayhorn's things. He hadn't written "Lush Life" yet.
Oh, I heard he wrote "Lush Life when he was in high school.

He may have, but we didn't play it. We played "A Train" and "My Little Brown Book." But see, "Lush Life" is more a tone poem. You don't jam anything on "Lush Life"; you play it from beginning to end. It's a complete story.
And you were playing it on the piano here a little while ago, and I was loving it. It's beautiful.
Oh, yeah. Well, "Lush Life" is one of the greatest compositions ever written, you know. It's a complete story.
That's what Billy is supposed to have shown or played for Duke when they first met, which is why Duke said... You know, he had plans for Billy when he heard that.
I didn't know that. But I do know what I just told you.
